source.title: Pretrained Generative Language Models as General Learning Frameworks for Sequence-Based Tasks

record.file_problem: None; the full paper text, including appendices, is present.
record.tranche_reason: The study evaluates downstream task performance across model sizes and pretrained models, using task-output metrics rather than held-out cross-entropy or the original scaling-law method.
record.gate_note: The paper does not measure held-out pretraining loss, fit power laws, test extrapolation from small runs, or optimize parameter/token allocation for fixed compute. Rows below cover its own downstream-task outcomes across pretrained model sizes and model choices. Results it cites about scaling laws or prior methods are not recorded as rows.
record.test_reason: The study gives its own downstream results, exact match on SMILES-to-IUPAC, across model sizes. Fine-tuned OPT runs at 125M, 350M and 1.3B, and zero-shot base models from 125M to 70B, bear on V6 in a new, niche task setting. It fits no power law, measures no pretraining loss, and has only three fine-tuned sizes, so 'predictably' is not tested.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors conclude that small pretrained generative LMs (1M–1.3B) can be fully fine-tuned with 10k–1M instruction examples into specialist models reaching near-prior-art results on SMILES-to-IUPAC. Outcomes depend on model size, model family, data amount, epochs (diminishing after 20–30) and instruction formatting. They make no claims about loss power laws.
record.recipe_differences: This is a task-specific fine-tuning study using exact-match and text-similarity metrics, not a scaling-law fit to held-out cross-entropy or a compute-optimal allocation experiment.
record.method_sensitivity: Fine-tuned task performance varies with model size, pretrained model selection, fine-tuning data amount, epoch count, architecture, and data formatting; the paper also reports effects from generation beam size.

fits_no_version.finding: Among similarly sized TinyStories models fine-tuned on 1M examples, deeper models (8 layers) beat shallow ones (1–4 layers). This is a downstream metric, not pretraining loss.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Depth affects fine-tuned downstream performance at fixed parameter count.

fits_no_version.finding: Fine-tuned performance rises with the number of fine-tuning examples (Figure 2) and with epochs, plateauing after about 20–40 epochs (Figures 3–4). No power-law fit is made.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Fine-tuning data and epoch scaling for task performance.

record.problems: The evidence concerns one specialized task and output-based metrics rather than held-out loss. Several size-sweep values are shown only in figures, and the paper reports no error bars or confidence intervals for the main comparisons.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant results omitted. Other experiments on instruction formatting, epochs, adapters, inverse-task conversion, and generation settings were not included because they do not measure the scaling or downstream-scale relationships represented by the rows.

untested.parts: Whether gains are predictable, i.e. a fitted functional form or extrapolation; performance as a function of pretraining loss; other downstream tasks.
All of it: no held-out pretraining loss is measured.
All of it: no fits or extrapolation.
All of it: no compute-allocation sweep.
Pretraining loss at fixed parameter count. The TinyStories depth result is downstream and fine-tuned only.
Power-law form under fine-tuning. Performance rises with fine-tuning data, but no fit is made and no loss is measured.
All of it: no exponents are fitted.

missing.what: OPT-125M fine-tuned on 1M examples reaches 44% exact match and BLEU 0.79. Seed variation is at most 2%.
Standard full fine-tuning at 100k examples: OPT-125M gets 0% exact match (BLEU 0.20), OPT-1.3B gets 21% (BLEU 0.63).
OPT-1.3B fine-tuned on 1M examples reaches mean BLEU 0.92. BLEU also rises with size in Figure 6.
Base TinyStories models (1M–33M) and phi-1_5 all score 0% exact match zero-shot.

record.verdict_notes: The evidence on V6 is narrow: one niche task, three fine-tuned OPT sizes, and size comparisons partly confounded with model family. The text says Bloom and SantaCoder outperformed OPT-1.3B, but Bloom's 68% exact match is below OPT-1.3B's 71%. The zero-shot null result reflects a task chosen to be impossible for base models.

versions.untested_parts: No held-out pretraining loss or loss-versus-parameters, tokens, or compute relationship is measured.
No power-law fit or prediction of larger-run loss from smaller runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token counts.
The paper compares architectures on a fine-tuned task, but does not measure loss at fixed parameter count.
Although it studies fine-tuning, it does not test whether the same power-law form holds for loss in another training regime or modality.
One cheminformatics task is evaluated using output-match and text-similarity metrics; the study does not test other downstream tasks or performance as a function of pretraining loss.
No scaling-law exponents or compute-optimal split are fitted or compared across fitting choices.

relationships.condition: After task fine-tuning: OPT 125M/350M/1.3B on identical data, and about 125M vs about 1.1B models across families
relationships.reason: Exact match rises with size: OPT 0%→21% at 100k and 44%→71% at 1M. At 1M, about 125M models reach 2–7% while about 1.1B models reach 68–75%. Only three sizes and no fit (opt-size-*, t2-* rows).
relationships.display_finding: OPT exact match increased from 0% to 21% at 100k examples and 44% to 71% at 1M; at 1M, approximately 125M models achieved 2–7% versus 68–75% for approximately 1.1B models.

relationships.condition: Zero-shot base models on an out-of-distribution task, OPT 125M–30B and Llama-2 7B–70B
relationships.reason: Exact match is 0% and BLEU 0 at every size up to 70B, and OPT edit distance does not improve with size (base-opt*, base-llama* rows). Scale alone gives no gain on this task.
relationships.display_finding: Exact match remained 0% and BLEU remained 0 through 70B, while OPT edit distance showed no improvement with size.

relationships.condition: Fine-tuned models at matched parameter count but different families or depth
relationships.reason: At 125M and 1M examples, GPT-neo gets 2%, GPT-2 7% and OPT 44%. At about 1.1–1.3B, Bloom gets 68%, OPT 71% and SantaCoder 75%. TinyStories-28M beats the 33M models. Size does not determine outcome (t2-*, tiny-28m).
relationships.display_finding: With 1M examples, 125M GPT-neo, GPT-2 and OPT achieved 2%, 7% and 44%; around 1.1–1.3B, Bloom, OPT and SantaCoder achieved 68%, 71% and 75%, while TinyStories-28M beat the 33M models.
